title: Acton teen accused of killing mom, brother ordered held without bail
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, charged with murdering his mother Sudha Venkatesan, 45, and brother Siddharth Aravind, 14, in Acton.
Crime scene showed signs of violent struggle; victims died from blunt force trauma, affirming homicide ruling.
Aravind arrested in Wayland driving his mother's car; facing multiple charges, including murder and vehicle theft.

title: Downtown Boston was buzzing in July. Here’s a look at the numbers.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Downtown Boston experienced a 10.5% increase in domestic foot traffic in July 2026 over July 2025.
Events like the World Cup and Sail Boston contributed to an economic boost in Downtown Boston.
Boston City Council is considering permanently extending bar hours and expanding social districts based on summer success.

title: 2 seriously injured in West End stabbing, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A man and a woman were seriously injured in a domestic stabbing incident in Boston's West End.
The incident occurred at 55 Causeway St., with police responding shortly after 11 a.m. on Thursday.
The man's injuries were self-inflicted and life-threatening, while the woman's injuries were not life-threatening.

title: Healey temporarily restricts kratom sales statewide
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts designates kratom as a Schedule I substance, citing a high potential for abuse and lack of medical use.
Governor Maura Healey's order on kratom sales takes effect after 14 days, lasting up to one year.
Massachusetts joins 14 states restricting kratom, with varying regulations across New England, including bans in Vermont and Connecticut.

title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich on Cape Cod was voted the best town by Boston.com readers, known for beaches and oyster specials.
Ogunquit, Maine, named the best beach town in New England, offers scenic seaside views and attractions.
The Deerfield Fair, New England's oldest family fair, will occur October 1-4 in Deerfield, New Hampshire.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving incident 2 nautical miles north-northwest of Sesuit Harbor on Wednesday.
The search and recovery involved Dennis, Barnstable, and Sandwich fire departments, along with U.S. Coast Guard aerial support.
Authorities pronounced the diver dead at Sesuit Harbor; the incident is under ongoing investigation.

title: Lindsay Clancy’s raw journal entries read in court
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Prosecutors requested access to logs of Lindsay Clancy's courthouse visitors during her trial, noting visits from individuals other than her lawyer.
Massachusetts State Police Trooper Joshua McKelligan testified about the crime scene and Clancy's medications during the trial.
Journal entries from Lindsay Clancy revealed her struggles with postpartum depression, anxiety, and parenting her children.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: The Westerly, Rhode Island beach house features a contemporary cottage style and was built in 1987.
The property spans 2,724 square feet, with 3 bedrooms and 3 full bathrooms.
The house has a private sewer, public water, and 2025 taxes amounting to $11,125.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 13, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: First Crush, a natural wine bar, opens mid-September 2026 at 259 Washington St., Somerville.
Johnny Boy turns its Filipino-inspired sandwich popup into a permanent location at 300 Summer St., Seaport.
Jūni, offering to-go omakase sets, opens a ten-seat sushi counter at 1211 Hancock St., Quincy.

title: 3 concerning trends from Red Sox’ 5-game losing skid
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox have lost five consecutive games, averaging just 2.8 runs per game over this skid.
The bullpen is struggling with Tyron Guerrero and Aroldis Chapman allowing critical runs in recent games.
Boston's defense faltered with key errors by Willson Contreras and Caleb Durbin, affecting their recent performances.
